title: VoltPilot v2 Flow Graph
description: Editierbarer, versionierter Flow-Graph und Eingabe des Compilers. Knoten stammen aus dem VoltPilot-Katalog und werden über typisierte Ports und Trigger verbunden. Der Katalog enthält einen begrenzten Funktionsknoten sowie ausdrücklich geregelte generische Modbus-Knoten; deren Ausführungs- und Governance-Grenzen stehen in flow-graph.md. Dieses Schema prüft die Dokumentform. Ports, Zyklen, Claims, Berechtigungen und Herkunftsregeln benötigen zusätzlich die semantischen Validatoren. Vertragsversion: 1.0.

flow_id.description: Stable identity of the flow across versions.

flow_version.description: Monotonically increasing version. Editing an active flow creates a NEW draft version; the active version keeps running until the new one is activated.

runtime.description: Where this flow executes (D8: one flow model, two runtimes). Node catalog entries declare which runtimes they support; the validator refuses a node outside its runtime.

site_id.description: The site an edge flow belongs to (required for runtime=edge). Cloud/portfolio flows scope by tenant instead.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of THIS version. Informative snapshot in the document; the AUTHORITATIVE state machine lives in the platform API (see flow-graph.md): draft -> simulated (a recorded simulation run exists) -> active (validated + compiled + deployed; at most one active version per flow) -> retired.

origin.description: OPTIONAL provenance marker of a GENERATED flow (D-19): present exactly when the platform derived this document from another source of truth. SERVER-STAMPED ONLY - the flow save API refuses customer documents carrying it, so origin can never be forged to unlock generated-only node types. Which kinds a generated-only type unlocks is CATALOG DATA (`generated_origin`), never a constant: today `consumer-policy` owns vp.consumer.reactive and its compiler-stamped override, `modbus-device` owns vp.modbus.switch, `mqtt-device` owns vp.mqtt.read and `http-device` owns vp.http.read. A type may name SEVERAL kinds (`generated_origin` is a string OR a list): the level-2 companion vp.soc.derive belongs to `mqtt-device` AND `http-device`, because the state of charge is derived from the standard channels and does not care which level-1 read type delivered them. Beyond that they are NOT interchangeable - a level-1 read type is valid only under ITS OWN origin kind. A generated flow is not separately editable; portals open the owning builder instead. Four sources exist: a consumer policy (docs/verbrauchssteuerung.md §13.2), a self-built Modbus device (vp-modbus-baukasten-k6 §2.2) and a self-connected battery read over MQTT or over an HTTP/JSON endpoint (vp-deye-diybms-luecke-l5 §3.2b). The `kind` discriminates; each shape is closed, so a document may never mix the vocabularies.

oneOf.title: mqtt-device
oneOf.description: The generated flow of ONE self-connected battery read over a LOCAL MQTT broker (P5 Ebene 1, Konzept vp-deye-diybms-luecke-l5 §3.2b): exactly one vp.mqtt.read node whose user-defined field mapping turns the source's topics into the standard battery channels, plus - since P5b (Ebene 2) and only when the battery HAS a state of charge - one vp.soc.derive node wired to its output, which derives soc_pct (taken over, from the OCV curve, or counted from charge) and publishes it together with its origin soc_source_code. It unlocks those two generated-only types and is the only kind that does - there is deliberately no free MQTT block while the mapping UI (P5d) is still to come. Like the modbus-device kind it marks the flow as platform-owned (portals open the battery assistant, not the flow editor) and names the definition version the mapping was compiled from - which IS flow_version.

point_id.description: The measurement_point (component) this read flow belongs to.

definition_version.description: measurement_point.definition_version the mapping was compiled from; it IS the flow_version, so a rolled-back definition redeploys its own mapping.

oneOf.title: http-device
oneOf.description: The generated flow of ONE self-connected battery read over an HTTP/JSON endpoint in the customer LAN (P5 Ebene 1 "HTTP/JSON", Konzept vp-deye-diybms-luecke-l5 §3.2b): exactly one vp.http.read node that GETs one JSON document per tick and whose user-defined value paths turn its fields into the SAME standard battery channels as the MQTT read type, plus - only when the battery HAS a state of charge - the same vp.soc.derive node wired to its output. It is the exact sibling of mqtt-device and exists as its OWN kind for one reason: a level-1 read type must never be valid under another transport's origin, or a forged mqtt-device document could unlock an HTTP fetch. The auth SECRET is deliberately NOT part of this document (it travels in the entity registry push, driver.connection.auth_secret) - a flow document is readable through the portal API, and a credential in it would be a credential in the browser. Like the other device kinds it marks the flow as platform-owned (portals open the battery assistant, not the flow editor) and names the definition version the mapping was compiled from - which IS flow_version.

point_id.description: The measurement_point (component) this read flow belongs to.

definition_version.description: measurement_point.definition_version the mapping was compiled from; it IS the flow_version, so a rolled-back definition redeploys its own mapping.

oneOf.title: modbus-device
oneOf.description: The generated flow of ONE self-built Modbus device: its read plan (Einheitsmodell Stufe 3) plus - once the customer has passed the guided switch test and confirmed the physical effect - the generated executor vp.modbus.switch (Einheitsmodell Stufe 4). This origin therefore DOES unlock a generated-only type, and it is the only kind that unlocks it; there is deliberately no free Modbus WRITE block. It also marks the flow as platform-owned so portals open the device assistant instead of the flow editor, and it names the definition version the plan was compiled from.

point_id.description: The measurement_point (component) this read flow belongs to.

definition_version.description: measurement_point.definition_version the plan was compiled from; it IS the flow_version, so a rolled-back definition redeploys its own plan.

nodes.description: Node instances. Types come from the versioned VoltPilot node catalog (namespaced vp.<domain>.<name>); parameters are validated against the catalog type's parameter schema by the platform validator.

type.description: Catalog type id, e.g. vp.entity.read, vp.entity.control, vp.strategy.market, vp.strategy.peakshaving, vp.price.dayahead, vp.logic.threshold, vp.logic.and, vp.schedule.window, vp.notify.push.

type_version.description: Semver of the catalog type this instance was built against. The compiler resolves the concrete implementation; flow-artifact carries the resulting minimum palette/runtime versions.

parameters.description: Type-specific parameters (validated against the catalog type's parameter schema). entityRef parameters reference entities by registry id.

claims.description: EXPLICIT control claims of this node: which entity actuations it drives (filled by the editor from the catalog type + parameters, so exclusive-resource validation works generically without knowing every type's parameter schema). Only action/strategy nodes carry claims; read nodes never do. Claim unit = the ENTITY (one controlling flow per entity - command types are not split across owners).

commands.description: The command vocabulary subset this node emits for the entity (edge-desired vocabulary).

delegated.description: true = a strategy node delegating the entity to the cloud co-optimizer (the plan will command it, class 'market'); false/absent = a direct action node emitting class-'flow' desires. Both are claims on the same exclusive resource - a delegated and a direct claim on one entity conflict.

edges.description: Directed, port-to-port connections. Port NAMES are strings; port TYPES (timeseries, number, bool, price, plan, event, entityRef) are declared by the catalog node type - the validator resolves and checks compatibility (flow-graph.md).

feedback.description: Declares an INTENTIONAL cycle (e.g. hysteresis on a previous output). Validation: the graph with all feedback edges removed must be acyclic; a feedback edge's value is the PREVIOUS evaluation's output (one-step delay), so evaluation always terminates.

triggers.description: What causes (re-)evaluation. Evaluation is single-threaded per flow, non-reentrant, bounded by the runtime's evaluation timeout (flow-graph.md).

kind.description: interval = fixed cadence; value-change = a watched port/entity channel changed beyond deadband; slot-boundary = the platform slot grid ticked (slot_minutes, aligned with the plan); event = a named platform event (e.g. plan-received, entity-offline, entity-online).

source.description: value-change only: the watched output port.

deadband.description: value-change only: minimum absolute change to fire (0/absent = any change).

event.description: event only: the platform event name.
